lines.text: What are they for?
From who?
I deliver brakes. I don't fix them.
Ask.
You don't have to tell me anything. But if you want to, I'm not going to repeat it. Not to him, not to anyone.
I'd stay out of it. Nobody ever got hurt by not asking.
lines.direction: Gently. It's not cruelty; it's fear.

lines.text: I won't.
I'll bring it back.
You didn't know it was the last time.
The box that doesn't say taxes.
lines.direction: Alone in a dusty storage unit. Light finger on a taped box.

lines.text: "Eddie is wrong. Again." "Eddie is wrong, but he is right about the brakes." This is Danny's handwriting.
lines.direction: Reading, slowly, a small, human laugh at the margin notes.

lines.text: "Berth Nine. Pickup 11 PM. Do NOT put the date on it. E. says it's a bad idea. It is." And a name. Not a name. Initials. R.
lines.direction: Quieter. Turning to the last ticket.

lines.text: Like she has opinions.
Why did you keep it?
What was the joke?
I will.
Lucille said it's not your fault.
I was going to ask for a wrench.
I like the window.
Different how?
She sounds like Lucille.
Not yet.
He looks like a Gerald.
You're making it weird.
It isn't.
The door's open.
lines.direction: Level. A little too tired to be polite.

lines.text: Dale sent me. He said you might need a driver.
He sold my room twice. So, desperate.
Non-refundable. Of course it is.
lines.direction: Flat, tired, almost amused at how bad this is.

lines.text: Thirty-eight dollars, a car that shudders on left turns, and a garage on Third. Fine. Third it is.
Tony didn't show up. I'm Ash. I'm delivering the truck for Eddie.
I don't know. I met Eddie ten minutes ago.
No. It's smooth.
What's the catch?
lines.direction: Careful. Not wanting to sound desperate.

lines.text: How much?
Ash.
lines.direction: A beat. Then offering the name.

lines.text: For now.
lines.direction: Not unfriendly. A closed door with a polite note on it.

lines.text: He asked about the previous owner. And a dent in the tailgate.
lines.direction: Hands over the signed paper. Watching Eddie.

lines.text: Sure.
That's a lot of advice for free.
The car. Possibly.
Thank you.
Somebody put a lot of work into this.
lines.direction: Walking around it. A little impressed in spite of themselves.

lines.text: The paperwork?
And which one do you think it is?
He said I shouldn't take it.
Understood.
It was fine.
I won't.
That's a lot for a car.
lines.direction: Careful. The money is heavy in the hand.

lines.text: And you know these people.
I'm told it's a skill.
But it pays.
Does he always do that?
lines.direction: To Mara, once Eddie is out of earshot.

lines.text: Eight hundred.
You know him.
The paperwork on the car didn't match.
I did. I'll have it for you tonight.
It wasn't there, Darius. They cleared the rack before I got in.
lines.direction: Careful, lying with a straight face.

lines.text: Darius sent me. For a case in Warehouse 14.
He said it was.
Cleared by who?
It's getting to be everybody's business, Walt.
lines.direction: Dry. Giving him the out and the push at once.

lines.text: And if the case isn't there?
Partial shipping manifest. Handwritten notes. And a company name.
lines.direction: Opening the case. Reading, a little breathless.

lines.text: Alder Point Development. Consulting fees. Payable to King Haulage.
lines.direction: Slow, reading it off. Unhappy about it.

lines.text: That's not paperwork. That's a rope.
lines.direction: Closing the case. Fast, a decision.

lines.text: Container tag says PAC-4471.
lines.direction: Muttering, crouched by a container, reading it.

lines.text: Paperwork on the door says Berth Nine. This is not Berth Nine. This container was never supposed to be here.
lines.direction: A flat, careful read. Quiet thinking aloud.

lines.text: Okay. Okay, there you are.
lines.direction: Pulling a latch, finding a hard case behind a pallet. Low.

lines.text: I found it.
lines.direction: Lays the case on the bench. Tired, a bit shaky.

lines.text: You know the name.
You never told me.
And am I?
He asked for it. I owe him a straight answer, or at least a quiet one.
I'll hold it. Nobody sees it until I know whose it is.
You've been looking for months. It's yours as much as mine.
lines.direction: Pushing the case across the bench.

lines.text: Is this a getaway?
Close.
Keep driving.
Two behind, one pulling up on the right.
Eddie's back room.
You're sure?
Why tell me?
You said you thought somebody was following you.
We find him. Before anyone else does. And we find out what he knows. You're not alone in this.
lines.direction: Steady, kind, not pretending to have more than they have.

lines.text: You should have told me sooner. We both could have been dead at that beach.
lines.direction: Not cruel, but honest and a little hurt.

lines.text: Stay out of the next job. I'll handle it. You're too close to this.
Got it. It's lighter than I thought.
lines.direction: Pulling a damp canvas bag from the gap.

lines.text: I need a minute.
lines.direction: Slow, aware that the answer is a lever either way.

lines.text: A manifest. Alder Point, King Haulage, consulting fees. It's with someone I trust.
lines.direction: A slow breath. The wrong decision, said calmly.

lines.text: A shipping document. Mismatched container numbers. I'll know more when I know whose it is.
Nothing yet. I'd like to know whose side the evidence is on before I tell you what it says.
Eddie. I need you to look at this and tell me I'm wrong.
lines.direction: Quietly, putting the photograph on the bench.

lines.text: It's a blue pickup with a replaced tailgate and a fresh paint job. It looks like the one I delivered to Walt.
Who was it?
You remember the dent.
Okay. I won't drag you in.
lines.direction: Quiet. Putting the photograph back in the envelope.

lines.text: Somebody who writes the incident report.
I didn't know it was him.
Then that's where we look.
You said facts.
So you're a good cop with bad bosses.
Who told you about rack nine?
The incident report says rack nine?
You can do that.
A blue pickup. At night. A plate, partly covered.
lines.direction: Quiet. Opening the box and finding the photograph.

lines.text: "Berth Nine. Never reported."
And this?
lines.direction: Lifting a small cassette recorder, sealed in a bag. Frowning.

lines.text: I was hoping so.
I haven't spent it.
It was. Mostly.
Priya. She's the only one who wrote a word.
You keep them. You know the city better than I do.
lines.direction: Pushing the folder into her hands.

lines.text: We need someone with a badge. He can open doors we can't.
Or he isn't. I have to know.
I met a woman who said it was perfectly safe until somebody started making it dangerous.
I'll think about it.
lines.direction: Quiet. The envelope is heavier than it looks.

lines.text: No.
lines.direction: Pushing the envelope across the table with one finger. Level.

lines.text: Twenty thousand is a lot of reasons to listen. I'll consider myself advised.
lines.direction: Smooth. Not quite a lie, not quite the truth.

lines.text: I'm not here to buy.
This isn't an assessment. It's a sale option. With a thirty-day clause.
You'll want to read this slowly.
Not yet. Maybe not for a while. Keep it safe.
Which lender?
Purchase orders. Wharf Street, every unit. And a payment schedule. Alder Point Development to King Haulage, monthly. "Consulting: public safety."
There's a cross reference. PAC-4471.
Who do I call?
lines.direction: Out of breath. Weighing a call and a risk.

lines.text: A place to hide, and somebody who isn't afraid.
They're going to look there.
Darius is going to keep coming. We can't hide in a back room for the rest of our lives.
lines.direction: Standing at the window. Barely audible.

lines.text: Darius. It's Ash. You gave me eight hundred dollars. I'm giving you a week. Leave Mara's brother out of this, and leave Eddie's door alone.
lines.direction: Dialling. Cold, level, speaking to a recording of a man.

lines.text: Darius. I have half of what you want. I'll trade it for the people I care about.
lines.direction: Smooth. Playing the wrong card as well as it can be played.

lines.text: Let him wonder.
lines.direction: Putting the phone down on the sill. No call.

lines.text: Eddie. The truck in the photograph.
You didn't know.
I'm sorry.
They know about Mateo.
I made some bad ones. And some good ones. I'm going to need you to tell me which is which.
You're leaving.
Give me one more chance.
You said Darius wanted to say thank you.
lines.direction: Level, taking in the lot. Four dark cars where there were none.

lines.text: Jojo. Whose cars are those?
Okay.
You're not my friend, Darius.
Don't.
He was right. It was everybody's business.
lines.direction: Quiet. Standing in the doorway. Looking at the thermos on the step. It takes a while.

lines.text: He left us the log. I'll make it count.
lines.direction: Folding the envelope into a pocket. A low, flat promise, to nobody.

lines.text: Three options. A detective with a badge we can trust, or a reporter who prints the truth, or we hold it, and use it as leverage.
She will do it right. Slow, but right.
It's a risk. If he buries it, we know for certain. If he doesn't, it gets read by someone with power.
lines.direction: Level. It sounds sounder than it is.

lines.text: Then she has to be fast.
It's the only thing that keeps anyone alive. As long as nobody has it, nobody has to kill us for it.
You were. You stayed.
Walt, stay inside.
You don't fish, Walt.
You asked about the dent on the tailgate. The first day. Why?
What's in the envelope?
Rowan. Sloane. Darius.
You're saying it now.
lines.direction: Putting a hand on his shoulder.

lines.text: You were quick.
You don't have to come, Eddie.
Fair.
You tried to have me killed.
Danny Vale.
And you let Eddie believe he left town.
It still doesn't make it okay.
It's over, Darius.
You're going to say it all on the record. All of it. In front of someone you can't buy.
Walk. Leave Port Alder. If I see you again, I won't be asking.
This is for Danny.
lines.direction: Cold. Not loud. This is a decision they will remember every day.

lines.text: It suits it.
You're leaving?
That's fair.
Where will you go?
I have a place in a high building. A car. A job nobody can explain.
I know.
It's a beautiful view.
lines.direction: Alone at a very high window. The city spread out below like a light fixture. A voice that has stopped fighting.

lines.text: I don't know why I can't stop thinking about the sign on the garage.
Darius got out of town. Sloane's lawyers made sure of it. I used to think I was the only person in this city who could say no.
There was an exit. I think I drove past it.
lines.direction: A tired breath. The title of the story, said aloud for the first time.

lines.text: No.
I'm sorry.
Where are we going?
I wouldn't ask.
Last exit.
lines.direction: On the quay, watching the glow on the water. Low.

lines.text: You were the voice on the tape.
And now?
You keep copies. You always keep copies. Bring them.
I'm not your conscience.
You're alone.
No. Everything goes to people who can print it and prosecute it. Including this conversation.
lines.direction: Quiet. Firm. A decision that costs them something.

lines.text: It's been recording since the lobby.
lines.direction: Holding up a phone, the call light red.

lines.text: Fifty thousand. A clean record. I walk away and the paper never leaves my hands.
lines.direction: Slow. The words come out smoother than they feel.

lines.text: I know.
No deal. No reporter. Nobody gets any of it.
lines.direction: Very quiet. A decision made a long way down.

lines.text: You said it yourself, Mr. Sloane. It's only paper.
It's open. Somebody opened it.
lines.direction: Working the latch with a bar. Quiet.

lines.text: Ledgers. Boxes of them. Signed contracts. Hard drives. Everything, all of it, in one place.
lines.direction: Inside, a steel cabinet. Flat, unbelieving.

lines.text: Take what we can carry.
That sounds about right.
Why tell me?
Broken windows, fire damage, police tape. Nothing in the report. Not one word.
lines.direction: At the Wharf Street shops. Quiet.

lines.text: Locks cut, boxes opened. Somebody has been through here since the report was filed. Recently.
Fresh forklift tracks and a gate log with a page torn out. Dana was right. Every single report is wrong in exactly the same way.
What do you want to do?
Where is the money going?
She didn't say it to your face?
What are you carrying for them?
Mateo. Mara says you carry a bag very well. Those were Darius's words. Not hers.
Stop. Tell them you're sick. Tell them whatever you want. Your sister is the only one in this city who wants nothing from you.
Keep carrying. Tell me what you see. Don't be a hero. Just remember.
lines.direction: Careful. It is a cold thing to ask.

lines.text: Of leaving?
Go. Take Mateo and go. You've earned the map on your wall.
I'd like you to stay. Not because I need you to. Because this city has been shaped by people who left.
I can't be the reason you stay or go. That's not fair to either of us.
lines.direction: Careful. It comes out colder than it is.

lines.text: Mostly?
Lucille, get down.
And you want me to be the first.
It's about Wharf Street. We're collecting signatures against the buyout.
lines.direction: Talking to a stranger off-screen. Neutral and friendly.

lines.text: Thank you. You've done more than you know.
lines.direction: Taking the pen back with a small smile.

lines.text: Environmental waiver, signed, dated. The date is a Sunday. Nobody signs a waiver on Sunday.
lines.direction: Squinting at a laminated notice, taking a photograph. Quiet.

lines.text: And it's signed by a man who died in March.
Hey, it's Dale, about the room on Cedar. So, little bit of news. My cousin showed up this morning with cash in hand and, you know how it is, first come, first served.
lines.direction: Breezy, not sorry at all. Voicemail energy.

lines.text: Your deposit? That's a non-refundable retainer. It says so in the text I sent. Which you didn't read, because nobody reads them.
lines.direction: Bright and fast, getting ahead of the complaint.

lines.text: If you need work, try Vale Auto, over on Third. Eddie's always short a pair of hands. Say Dale sent you. Actually, don't. Just say you can drive. Good luck out there!
lines.direction: Throwing a crumb. Quick and vague.

lines.text: Please don't talk to me in front of the building. I mean it kindly.
lines.direction: Standing by her patrol car. Quiet, polite, glancing at the station.

lines.text: It's Dana Whitfield. I'll be at the harbor gate with three officers I trust. If you need police that aren't Detective Rowan's, that's us. Give me a signal.
lines.direction: On speaker. Careful, quiet, the sound of a person speaking from a stairwell.

lines.text: Detective Rowan. I'd like to ask you to come with me. Please.
lines.direction: Stepping out of the dark with two officers. Shaking a little, standing straight.

lines.text: You're Ash. I know you, because three different people told me not to talk to you.
lines.direction: Standing by her patrol car, keys turning in her fingers. Nervous and trying to look as though she is not.

lines.text: I'm Officer Whitfield. Dana. I've been on the street five years. I have a notebook and I have a photo of a logbook page that doesn't match it.
Detective Rowan's reports say that nothing happened at three addresses on nights when I was personally standing there watching things happen.
Because you're not on the force. Nobody can be sacked for talking to you.
Three places. The Wharf Street shops, the old Vale storage unit, and the Port Warehouse. Rowan's reports say "no incident". See what you see.
lines.direction: On the radio, businesslike. A list.

lines.text: Three sites. Three false reports. One signature. If this goes to the captain, it goes straight to Rowan. If it goes to Internal Affairs, I'm done before the end of the week.
lines.direction: Spreading photographs on the hood of the patrol car. Hands steady now.

lines.text: I want to keep a file. Real, properly documented, ready for the day someone who can act on it is willing to read it. And I want it to be me who kept it.
Thank you. For not telling me to leave it alone.
Ash! Ash, Ash, Ash. Port Alder has a very bad habit of buying cars it can't afford. I'd like to help one of them find a new home.
lines.direction: Warm, playful, theatrical. He is clearly enjoying it.

lines.text: Sports car, dealership lot, nice and visible. Bring it to the depot. The police might be a little curious. Don't be a hero. Be a driver.
Perfect. Not a scratch and a police chase to boot. You're wasted on Eddie, you know that? A man of your talents, fixing brakes.
lines.direction: Walking around the stolen car with his hands behind his back, grinning like a man at a gallery.

lines.text: See? That's why I like you. You're funny. Nobody's funny in Port Alder. They're just loud.
My favourite driver! Eat something. You look like you've been thinking. Thinking is how people lose weight.
lines.direction: Big, friendly, a hand on Ash's shoulder.

lines.text: There he is! The driver who doesn't crash!
lines.direction: Warm, loud, arriving with his arms open like this is a party.

lines.text: Look at that. Not a scratch. You know how many people I send out for a simple pickup, and what comes back? Dents. Excuses. One time, a goat. Don't ask.
lines.direction: Walks a circle around the car. Delighted by it, delighted by everything.

lines.text: I like him. Mara, I like him. Mr. Eddie's got himself some good hands. Come. Come in the shade. Jojo, get this person a cold drink.
lines.direction: A big laugh, a hand on Ash's shoulder. It lands lightly and stays.

lines.text: Eight hundred. Don't argue, it's embarrassing. Here is my one rule, my friend, and it's free. Port Alder rewards the people who get things done and don't ask what they're getting done. I'm a very generous man to people like that.
lines.direction: Counting bills with a showman's flourish, putting them into Ash's hand without being asked.

lines.text: It's not for the car. It's for the quiet.
lines.direction: Warm. Perfectly sincere. That's what makes it unsettling.

lines.text: Hm.
lines.direction: The smile stays. The eyes follow the police car, steady and unhurried. He says nothing until it is gone.

lines.text: Port Alder police. Always on time and never in the right place. Come back soon, Ash. Mara, a word.
lines.direction: Back in the joke, as if nothing happened.

lines.text: Ash! You're breathing! I've been telling everyone you're a legend. Did you get my case?
lines.direction: Warm, genuinely curious. Fishing, with a smile in his voice.

lines.text: Wonderful. Wonderful. See? That's all this is. Nothing has to be hard. You're a good man, Ash. Nobody ever gave me a reason to doubt you.
lines.direction: A big, delighted laugh with no tension in it at all, which is very much worth noticing.

lines.text: That's strange. Because it was supposed to be. Hm.
lines.direction: A very small pause. The smile does not leave his voice. It sounds slightly less like a person.

lines.text: It's fine. It's paperwork. I'll sort it out. Get some rest, friend. We'll talk soon.
lines.direction: Warm again, rolling over it. A joke, an invitation.

lines.text: Ash! My favourite driver. Are you sitting? Don't sit. This is a standing kind of job.
lines.direction: Warm, friendly, speaking from a car. Treats it like a favour between friends.

lines.text: There's a sealed hard case in Warehouse 14, down at the port. It's mine, it's paperwork, it's boring. A shipment leaves tonight and the case is going with it by mistake. I'd like it to stay in Port Alder, with me, like a good citizen.
lines.direction: Easy, naming it as if it were nothing.

lines.text: See Walt Pruitt at the gate. He knows nothing and loves it. Tell him it's for me.
lines.direction: A little joke to cover the weight.

lines.text: It will be. Be quick, be polite, and be home for dinner.
lines.direction: A fraction too fast, still cheerful.

lines.text: ...and the harbor squad? They're covered?
lines.direction: Recorded, hissy. Warm, mid-laugh, a little drunk on his own cleverness.

lines.text: That's why I love working with professionals.
That's fine. I like a man who knows what he wants. A week is a very long time.
lines.direction: Voice message, recorded. Lazy and warm and terrifying in the exact same breath.

lines.text: Now we're talking. Business is just talking with better manners.
Ash. Don't run. It's undignified. I've sent some friends to bring you home.
lines.direction: On the phone. Still warm. Every word relaxed, and not a trace of a smile left under it.

lines.text: See, that. That's what I can't forgive. Who gave you your first eight hundred dollars? Who put your name in the right ears? Who let you walk into my yard like family?
lines.direction: Soft. Hurt, almost, in a way that makes it worse.

lines.text: You went to Mara. You went to a journalist, or you're about to. You took a thing that belongs to me and showed it to people who don't love this city the way I do.
lines.direction: A low, patient breath. He is being very reasonable.

lines.text: How is Mara's brother? Mateo, isn't it? Seventeen. Lovely boy. He carries a bag very well.
lines.direction: Gently, as if he were asking about the family.

lines.text: I'm not threatening, Ash. I'm telling you about the weather. It's about to change.
lines.direction: The warmth drains from the voice all at once. Flat.

lines.text: You know, I really did like you.
lines.direction: Sitting on a crate on the quay with a bottle of something expensive, no tie, no smile. The warmth is gone. What's left is just tired.

lines.text: I tried to have you stopped. It's a different department.

Danny found a ledger he shouldn't have. Danny asked Sloane's people the wrong questions. And my crew, on my order, which I'll say once because I'm an honest man at least about this, made sure he stopped asking.
lines.direction: A very long beat. He doesn't look away.

lines.text: Everyone needs a version they can live with.

Listen to me. You think this is a morality play. It is not. Everybody in this city is compromised. Eddie fixed my trucks. Mara drove my cars. The cops take my envelopes. And Victor Sloane pays me to be a monster so he can stand on a stage and be the hero. I'm not the cancer, Ash. I'm the symptom.
lines.direction: Standing now. The charisma returns, thin as paint.

lines.text: It doesn't have to be okay. It only has to be true.
Jojo. Not you too.
You want to talk about okay? Come and get me.
lines.direction: Suddenly bright, suddenly cruel, a snap decision. He slides into his car.

lines.text: Well. That's quite a rear bumper you've got.
lines.direction: Sitting on the kerb beside his wrecked car, bleeding from the forehead. Not laughing. Almost relieved.

lines.text: Is it. Say what you're going to do. I'd rather hear it from a person than a siren.
I never could stand a good audience. Fine. Let's do it properly.
lines.direction: A very dry, very tired smile.

lines.text: You're going to regret that. I'll try to disappoint you as little as possible.
lines.direction: A thin, surprised breath, and then, a little startled by it, a real smile.

lines.text: Of course it is.
lines.direction: Barely audible. He has no more jokes.

lines.text: Port Alder's built for this, you know. Every road leads to somebody who owes me.
lines.direction: Over the radio, laughing, driving fast, enjoying himself in a thin, terrible way.

lines.text: All units, silent alarm at the Port Warehouse complex, Warehouse 14. Anonymous caller reports a break-in. Units responding, please advise.
Dispatch to Unit twelve. You are the first in, report on arrival.
lines.direction: Same flat tone, repeating after a pause.

lines.text: Alder Point. "A waterfront for everyone." Mr. Victor Sloane, who sounds like a man you'd meet in a very expensive elevator, says it's for everyone.
lines.direction: Rolling out the name like a man ordering wine in a haunted house.

lines.text: Wharf Street gets "relocated," which is a word that means "a van arrives." Lucille at the corner mart has been selling milk on that street since before you could legally own a sandwich.
And Sloane sends her an ENVELOPE. You know who sends envelopes? Villains and grandmas. And my grandmother was not a villain.
Over a casserole. Context matters, Mags.
A lighthouse with arms. That's not a development. That is a warning.
A source inside the department, whom I'll call Cheryl, because that is her name, tells me one of our detectives has been "writing his own incident reports."
Cheryl says this fella talks like a terms-and-conditions page. "Let's be precise." Folks, anyone who says "let's be precise" at a party has never once been invited back.
That's not a man. That is a rider on a contract. Rollo, you've said more tonight than you have since the fish thing.
We will never talk about the fish thing.
Burn the archive.
Lorraine. You sound exactly like Mags.
Lorraine, what's on your mind tonight?
Controversial. Bold. Lorraine, you are a brave woman, and a possibly invented one.
Lorraine, hold, please. ... We lost Lorraine. She's gone where all the good callers go. The other line.

Update from the public car park, where last night a gathering of gentlemen in matching dark sedans "discussed parking." Witnesses describe it as the most coordinated thing to happen in a car park since never.
IN UNISON, Mags. They signalled. That's not crime, that's choreography. I want to see the dance.
A spot! Folks, that's the oldest war in the world. "That's my spot." They've been doing it since the Romans.
What's suitable for a car park, Mags? Four? Five? A brisk shuffle?
Then I stand corrected. I've been driving like a man in a hurry for years.
Folks, the Ledger published the Alder Point investigation. Seven pages. I've read four. The rest are in a font I associate with divorces.
And let the record show, I called it. I called it eleven years ago.
It was fraud AND a shipment of left shoes. I contain multitudes.
Whoever you are, listener, you magnificent weirdo, Gulliver's will send you a mattress. Previously enjoyed.
It's the thought, Rollo.
Alder Point is open to the public. I went. It's a fence. With a gift shop. The gift shop sells the fence. In miniature.
It's a lovely fence! And the investigation we were all so excited about? Gone. Like a sandwich on a quay.
Rich, mysterious, and I bet he owns a robe. I envy him with the part of me that's a coward.
I'm saying it at the beginning. Now I'm free.
The container yard fire is still going. The mayor calls it "a learning opportunity." The insurance companies call it "a bigger learning opportunity."
lines.direction: Over the sound of a distant siren he is clearly enjoying.

lines.text: Of course you did.
Is it Gerald?
Gerald has the evidence! Rollo, zoom in! GERALD HAS THE EVIDENCE!
Of course he did. He's represented.
lines.direction: Sinking back, a man at peace with the universe.

lines.text: Now, the city council, bless their laminated hearts, is floating a fog tax.
Fee, tax, fog. Same shape. Residents who "benefit from fog" will pay eleven dollars a month.
Ambience. Mystery. Plausible deniability when you miss your exit. Councilman Tibbets says fog is, quote, "a municipal asset we've been giving away for free."
You want to tax weather, Tibbets, start with the weather you caused. The rain that fell on my toast. Billing department, are you there.
Then we're taxing the drawer.
lines.direction: A beat. Then, with full resolve.

lines.text: Quick personal update. This morning on the quay, a seagull took my entire sandwich. Not a bite. The sandwich, the wax paper, my dignity.
lines.direction: Wounded. A man about to explain a grudge.

lines.text: I extended a hand of friendship, Rollo, and he responded with a hostile takeover.
I owe a bird. Folks, sit with that. I sat with it for six hours, and I came out the other side a changed man. No. Same man. Angrier at bread.
Form eleven-B, "Complaint Against Wildlife With A Union." They're represented, folks. They have a rep. His name is Gerald. He is also a gull.
He looked at me like a man who bills by the hour.
Shots reported at North Point Lighthouse last night. Residents describe "a significant amount of noise and one unusually motivated seagull."
Union professionals. Bullets flying, light stays on. That is the dedication I want in a plumber.
There's always a thermos.
Good. Good! Somebody give that man a sandwich. Not a gull.
Rollo. Kill the sound effects.
lines.direction: Quiet. The act has gone out of him. This is the other man, the one under the show.

lines.text: There was a man out there. A dockworker. Folks, I make jokes about this city. The fog, the pigeons, the councilmen. And I'll keep making them, because that is the job. But a man who kept a logbook for twenty years and did the right thing late, he is gone. Mags, play the quiet one.
Then everybody just be quiet. Ten seconds.
Okay. Thank you. We'll be right back.

You are listening to Harbor AM eleven-ninety, the Dead Air Hour, where the dead air is the content and the content is, frankly, also dead. I'm Duke Pelletier. It's a beautiful night in Port Alder, I'm told. I haven't been outside since Tuesday.
lines.direction: Rolling, gravelly, delighted with himself. A man who has been awake for thirty hours and considers it a talent.

lines.text: Rollo is our camera guy. Say hello to the camera, Rollo.
Great energy. Rollo films this show for the video stream. We have four viewers.
And one is a man in Duluth who I believe is lost.
Everybody's asking, Duluth. Everybody's asking.
lines.direction: Leaning into the mic, tender, as if to the man himself.

lines.text: Housing news. A landlord on Cedar Street named Dale rented the same room to two different people. And a cousin.
lines.direction: Gleeful, the way a man is when a story contains a villain he can pronounce.

lines.text: A hybrid arrangement. It's a room, Dale! It's a room with three people in it and a lie!
Port Alder real estate, folks. If you can find it, you can lose it to a cousin.
This segment is brought to you by Gulliver's Discount Mattresses. Do you sleep? Gulliver's has a mattress for that. Do you not sleep? Gulliver's has a mattress for THAT.
lines.direction: The golden, trusted voice of a man reading something he has never read before.

lines.text: Enjoyed by WHO, Mags? That is a love story I did not ask for.
That's not a flaw, that's a feature. Gulliver's. Lie Down Somewhere. Offer not valid in fog.
Listener mail. A caller points out there are far too many grey sedans in Port Alder. Not variety. Not color. Sedans, grey.
Is it? Or is it ONE car, in a trench coat, going around very fast?
lines.direction: A man cracking open a case.

lines.text: That is exactly what the car wants you to say.
Four-four-seven-one. That's twice this week. That is either a clue or my birthday.
Then it's a clue!
Breaking news. Which I am legally required to say is not breaking, it's lightly cracking. Port police responded to a silent alarm at the Port Warehouse complex in ninety seconds.
Ninety seconds! Folks, these are the same officers who took forty minutes to find a parade. A PARADE. It had a float.
My theory: the alarm called the police itself. From the inside. Smart alarm. Woke up one morning, felt something, dialed.
Mags. You can't just say normal things. We have a format.
Four-four-seven-one. Which is also my locker at the Y, which I will now be checking, with a flashlight and a lawyer.
Listener theory of the week. The Harbor Wheel. Is it a ride? Or is it, and I'm just asking questions, a very slow antenna?
lines.direction: Lowering his voice to a stage whisper that is louder than his normal voice.

lines.text: Were you looking at the city, Mags, or was the city looking at you?
That's what they WANT you to be doing.
Rollo. Rollo, that is a conspiracy with a MENU. Mags, put that on a mug.
We have a wheel and we have a pretzel. We're a brand.
You said you wouldn't drag me in.
lines.direction: In the doorway. Not looking at Ash. A man who has been rehearsing a request for days.

lines.text: I'm dragging myself. I kept every job ticket for twelve years. Danny filed them. His handwriting. They're in a storage unit by the industrial blocks. I haven't been in there since.
lines.direction: A long pause. His voice is almost too soft.

lines.text: There's a box that says TAXES on it. It doesn't say taxes. Don't tell anyone I said that.
He wrote "E. says it's a bad idea." I did say that. I did.
lines.direction: Holding the last ticket in two fingers. He doesn't turn it over until he has read it three times.

lines.text: And here's the part that's going to bother me for the rest of my life. I wasn't wrong. I just didn't stop him.
No. But I think I could have.
lines.direction: A small, careful breath, and, for the first time, he looks at Ash.

lines.text: There's a truck. Blue. You know the one. It's in Walt's yard at the docks. I'd like it back. Not for the money.
lines.direction: On the phone. Gruff, too casual, a man asking for a favour by pretending it isn't one.

lines.text: It's the only thing of his I can still fix.
How does she sound?
lines.direction: Over the phone. Stiff, quiet, trying not to ask.

lines.text: That's her. Bring her home.
You know, I fixed this. I fixed it wrong. I repaired every dent and not one thing that mattered.
lines.direction: Walking around the pickup, one palm flat on the hood. Not speaking for a while.

lines.text: Thank you for bringing her back.
There's one more thing. People who knew Danny. Not the docks. Not the crew. People who liked him. I realised I'd never asked any of them what they remembered.
lines.direction: On the phone. Rough. He has decided to say something and cannot yet say it.

lines.text: Lucille Ng. She says he fixed her delivery van for free for a year. She's been trying to tell me for five years. I kept finding reasons to be somewhere else.
He told that joke to me too. Every day. It never got better.
lines.direction: Standing at the end of the pier with the brass wrench keyring in his hand. A long silence.

lines.text: I'll believe her in a few years. But it's a start.
lines.direction: A short, wet laugh. He wipes his eyes and does not apologise.

lines.text: There. Everyone says to say goodbye. I'm just going to say I'm sorry I took so long.
lines.direction: Hanging the keyring on the rail, gently, and stepping back. Quietly.

lines.text: The garage is yours whenever you need it. Free. Parts too. I'll complain about it, but you'll never see a bill.
lines.direction: Turning, brisk, the old Eddie sliding back in.

lines.text: The coffee machine is broken. Don't take that personally. It's broken for everyone.
If you're going to ask about the job, no. If you're going to ask how I'm doing, also no.
Third drawer. Don't lose it. It's the only one I like.
You're still here. I keep expecting you to be a person who leaves.
Nobody likes the window.
Walt's been quiet. Walt is always quiet. But it's a different quiet.
lines.direction: Not turning round. Flat, the voice of a man who has been told too much and not enough.

lines.text: Like a man holding his breath.
I'm going to say his name every day. Danny. There. That's the exercise. The therapist is a woman called Pat. She's very good, she hates my jokes.
lines.direction: Quiet. He has been saying it to himself all morning.

lines.text: Everybody does.
There's a rumour you took Sloane's money. I told them it was a lie. Is it a lie?
Okay. Thank you for the honesty. I'm going to keep hoping that stays true.
lines.direction: Quiet. A longer silence than he usually allows.

lines.text: We're closed.
lines.direction: Muffled, half under a hood. Not looking up. Deadpan.

lines.text: The door's always open. It's the sign that lies. Sign says "closed" so people who want a quote go away. You want a quote?
lines.direction: Dry, patient, like he has explained this before.

lines.text: Dale.
lines.direction: A beat of silence. Surfaces slowly from under the hood.

lines.text: Dale owes me three hundred dollars and a transmission. When Dale starts sending people, he's either dying or desperate.
lines.direction: Wiping his hands on a rag. Faintly amused, faintly pained.

lines.text: Yeah. That sounds like Dale.
lines.direction: Finally looks at Ash. A small, dry exhale that is almost a laugh.

lines.text: Ash. Eddie. Quick thing: Walt's picky. Be polite, hand over the truck, get the signature. And if he asks you anything about the truck, you don't know anything.
lines.direction: On the phone, distracted, clanking in the background.

lines.text: Which, to be fair, you don't. So that part should be easy.
lines.direction: Adding it as a joke, hoping it lands as one.

lines.text: You look like somebody who could use a job. Lucky for you, I have a truck that needs driving.
lines.direction: Dry humour, distracted, pretending not to care.

lines.text: No catch. My usual guy didn't show up. He does that. I have a pickup that needs to be at the docks in the next hour, and I have a waiting list of exactly nobody.
Two hundred. Cash, when you get back. The blue pickup, out front. Keys are in it, because if somebody steals it, it's the most useful thing that ever happened to me.
lines.direction: Names a figure the way you'd name a weather report.

lines.text: I'm Eddie. Vale. It's on the sign, which is the only reason anybody gets it right.
lines.direction: Looks at Ash properly for the first time.

lines.text: Just Ash.
Fine. For now. Take it to the docks, find a man named Walt Pruitt, hand him the truck and the paperwork on the seat. Don't scratch it. Don't talk about the weather. Walt hates the weather.
lines.direction: Lets it go, which is a kindness. Back to business.

lines.text: Still got the truck? No. Walt's got the truck. You still have both arms. That's a good first day.
lines.direction: Glancing up from a clipboard. Dry.

lines.text: Walt asks everyone about everything. He once asked me where my shoes came from. It's a lonely port.
lines.direction: A fraction too quick. Light and dismissive.

lines.text: Two hundred. Take it. And a piece of advice, free, which is the only kind I give: this city is full of strange people. Most of them are just lonely. A few of them are not. You don't need to know which is which, you need to not ask.
lines.direction: Counts out the cash and puts it on the bench, not in Ash's hand.

lines.text: Where are you sleeping tonight?
lines.direction: Quiet, almost shy. Looking at the clipboard instead of Ash.

lines.text: There's a room out back. Cot, hot plate, a window that doesn't close. It's not charity. I need somebody to keep an eye on the place at night, and I'm too cheap to hire anybody I'd have to like.
Don't thank me. Thank the window. It lets in the cold, so you'll want to be tough.
lines.direction: Waves it off without turning around.

lines.text: She's older than she looks and louder than she should be. Brake pedal is honest. Horn is a liar.
lines.direction: Gesturing at the pickup with a wrench. Lightly mocking his own work.

lines.text: Somebody did. Get in. Seat's a little forward. You'll live.
Ash. Mara. Mara, Ash. Don't shake hands, it'll just make it official.
lines.direction: Not looking at anyone. Rag, wrench, reluctance.

lines.text: The call you got last night. The one I told you to ignore. That's Darius King's people. I'm not telling you to take it. I'm telling you it's a bad idea in a nice jacket.
lines.direction: Quieter. To Ash, not to Mara.

lines.text: It pays. That's the whole problem with it.
lines.direction: A tired breath. He has had this argument with himself for years.

lines.text: Nothing ever has. That's how you know it's about to.
Be careful about work from strangers. Strangers have reasons.
lines.direction: He goes. Over his shoulder, to Ash.

lines.text: Mara texted me you got paid.
lines.direction: Leaning in the doorway of the back room, arms folded. Soft, not accusing.

lines.text: Yeah. That's the number he opens with.
lines.direction: A short, quiet breath. He looks at the floor.

lines.text: Everybody who has a car in this city knows Darius King. Knowing him and owing him are two different things. Be the first kind.
lines.direction: Closing it down fast, but not rudely.

lines.text: Paperwork never matches. It's the only thing it's good at. Get some sleep.
lines.direction: Very still for half a second. Then he says it too evenly.

lines.text: It's a truck.
lines.direction: Wiping his hands. He looks, and stops wiping.

lines.text: It's that one. I did the tailgate. A big dent, shaped like a boot. I did the paint. I put the plates on. A man from the docks brought it in at two in the morning, paid cash, and asked me not to put the date on the ticket.
lines.direction: Very quiet. He puts the rag down, slowly, as if it might break.

lines.text: I don't remember. It was five years ago. You fix a hundred cars and you don't keep every face.
Yeah. I remember the dent.
lines.direction: Pause. His voice goes quieter, not louder.

lines.text: I need you not to involve me anymore. Whatever this is, I can't be in it. I have a garage. I have a mortgage. I have... I can't be in it, Ash.
lines.direction: Sharp, protective, a man pulling a door shut. He does not look up.

lines.text: Thanks.
Where are you? No. Don't tell me. Come to the garage. The back door's open.
lines.direction: Phone. Rough. He picks up on the first ring.

lines.text: Let them look.
lines.direction: Quiet, steady. The first time he has sounded certain about anything.

lines.text: They didn't come. Not yet.
lines.direction: Standing in the doorway of the back room with the lights off. He has closed the garage door and locked it. He talks to the floor.

lines.text: My brother's name was Danny. He was three years younger than me and he laughed at everything. We ran this garage together. Eleven years. Then Darius King showed up with a job that paid in a week what we made in a month.
lines.direction: Slow. Quiet. He sits down on the edge of the cot like his knees have stopped being reliable.

lines.text: I told him not to take it. He took it. The night he was supposed to come home, a man from the docks brought me that truck at two in the morning with the tailgate kicked in and a story about how Danny had left town. I fixed it. I repainted it. I put on the plates.
I didn't want to. There's a difference. For five years, I told myself he went to Florida. I even bought a map.
lines.direction: Very quiet. It is not an absolution.

lines.text: He didn't go to Florida.
Don't be. Be angry. I've been practising being sorry for five years. It never got me anywhere.
lines.direction: A short, rough breath. He wipes his face with the back of his hand, once.

lines.text: I closed the shop this morning. Put a note on the door. First time in eleven years the sign's been telling the truth.
lines.direction: Hauling the garage shutter down halfway, then leaving it. Dry, but steadier than we have heard him.

lines.text: These are Danny's. I've carried them for five years in case he came back for them. I thought I'd bring them. He'd want to be annoyed with me for coming.
lines.direction: A small, wry exhale. He holds up a ring of keys.

lines.text: You make it sound organised.
If this goes badly, tell them I told you so. In a nicer voice than I normally use.
lines.direction: From the back seat. Quiet, steady, a mechanic's opinion.

lines.text: Took a while to decide who to put on it.
lines.direction: Hanging a new, hand-painted sign above the garage door. It reads VALE & VALE AUTO. He does not turn around.

lines.text: I went to the harbor. First time in five years. Sat on the quay for an hour. Didn't say anything. I think that was the point.
They read Darius's statement on the news. I listened to the whole thing. He said Danny's name, in a courtroom. I didn't think I'd ever hear that.
You let him walk. I'm still angry about that. I'll be angry for a while. But I'm working on being angry out loud.
I heard what happened to Darius. I don't want to talk about it. I just want you to know that I know, and I'm still standing here.
The back room's still yours. If you want it. The window still doesn't close.
lines.direction: A last, dry line. It is the closest he will come to a hug.

lines.text: You're leaving.
lines.direction: The garage door half down. The sign over it is still the old one. He is cleaning a wrench he doesn't need to clean.

lines.text: You had the chance to say my brother's name out loud, in front of the whole city. And you took the money.
The room's empty. I'll leave the window open in case you ever want to climb back in.
lines.direction: Quiet. A different voice entirely: the one for people he has stopped expecting anything from.

lines.text: You didn't keep a copy.
lines.direction: Standing in the door of the garage as sirens carry across the city. He is holding an envelope. He does not look surprised.

lines.text: Danny would've liked the fire. He never could stand a ledger.
I'd have liked to hear his name, though. Once. In a room full of people. Out loud.
I know. Go on. Before they ask who lit it.
lines.direction: A small, honest nod. It does not forgive and it does not condemn.

lines.text: Ash. Go. I'll watch the mirrors.
lines.direction: Steady. His voice is a rock.

lines.text: Whose car is that?
lines.direction: Low, suspicious. Hand on the gate. Not an ordinary employee.

lines.text: Who's that?
Cruiser.
lines.direction: Under his breath, watching the road, nervous.

lines.text: ...and if you're just coming in off the coast road, welcome to Port Alder. Population: big. Parking: small. This is Marty Quill on Alder FM, and it is a very good evening to be somewhere else, or here, I guess. Here is fine.
lines.direction: Big warm radio voice, mid-sentence, selling the city.

lines.text: Traffic: the Harbor Bridge is moving. The highway is what we politely call "a conversation." If you're headed through the port, the gate guys are checking paperwork twice, so bring a book.
Sloane Development, everybody. Building what comes next, and demolishing what came before, but they don't put that on the radio. Here's something from a band that definitely doesn't exist.
lines.direction: Back to breezy, a little dry about the ad.

lines.text: This is Alder FM. We are interrupting our regular programming. The Port Alder Ledger has this morning published a seven-page investigation into the Alder Point redevelopment.
lines.direction: Warm radio voice gone quiet. Genuinely shaken, for once not performing.

lines.text: Police confirm that a senior detective has given a statement, and that warrants have been issued for Victor Sloane and for several officials.
Police confirm they are reviewing the documents. A senior detective is on leave. Warrants are reported to be issued for Victor Sloane.
And for once, folks, I have nothing funny to say.
Sloane Development, everybody. Building what comes next. We'll be right back after this word from a sponsor, which is also Sloane Development.
lines.direction: Flat. A man who knows what he is selling and has decided not to say it.

lines.text: This is Alder FM. Emergency crews are at the Port Alder container yard, where a fire has spread across the northern berths. Authorities believe that documents relating to the Alder Point project were among the material destroyed.
lines.direction: Raw, hushed, broadcasting while something terrible is still happening. No jokes.

lines.text: Victor Sloane's office has issued a statement. It says only: "We are deeply saddened."
You're listening to Alder FM. If you're stuck on the highway, relax. It's a very nice highway to be stuck on.
Port police have confirmed a break-in at a port warehouse and reported that, quote, nothing of value was taken. Unquote. Which is the best kind of break-in, if you ask a certain kind of person.
The Port Alder Ledger is promising a series on waterfront redevelopment. Sloane Development says it welcomes, quote, "any good faith inquiry."
Police are investigating a disturbance at the public car park this evening. Nobody has been hurt, the cars are, however, unrecognisable.
lines.direction: Flat. Reading what has been handed to him.

lines.text: Hey! Darius says you can do a collection run with me. Three shops, three envelopes. Nobody gets hurt, nobody gets hassled. We just say hi and take the thing. Easy.
lines.direction: Bright, a little too eager. He loves being asked.

lines.text: Darius is going to love this. He loves it when the envelopes are right.
lines.direction: Counting the envelopes, a little too carefully. He doesn't meet Ash's eye.

lines.text: Insurance. It's, like, protection. For the shops. You know, from stuff.
lines.direction: Fast, flat, the voice of someone lying to himself.

lines.text: That's the funny part.
Okay. Nice and calm. We say it's from Darius.
lines.direction: Hopping out of the car, whispering back through the window.

lines.text: See? Easy. Nobody even looked at us.
lines.direction: Back in the car, a small, nervous laugh.

lines.text: Can I ask you something? You're not going to tell Darius?
lines.direction: Alone, pacing between two trucks, not slowing when Ash walks up.

lines.text: If you found out something... bad. About him. About what we move. What would you do?
Okay. Okay. There's a container. I drove it. I'm not sleeping. If I ever need to call you, I'll call you.
lines.direction: A long, shaky breath. A young man putting something heavy down.

lines.text: Yeah. That's what I figured. Forget I asked.
lines.direction: Flat. The face of someone who has been given exactly the answer he feared.

lines.text: Hey! Sorry, I'm busy. I'm always busy. It's a thing I do now.

Hey. You don't know me. Somebody I work for heard Eddie's got a new driver who doesn't crash. Pays three times what Eddie pays. Talk to Eddie about it. He knows who I mean. Don't, uh, don't tell him I said that.
lines.direction: Voice message. Nervous, trying to sound relaxed and failing a little.

lines.text: It's fine, it's fine, they're with Darius. Hey. You're the new driver? I'm Jojo. I left you that message. Sorry about the message. I'm bad at messages.
lines.direction: Hurrying up, nervous energy. Cutting off whatever the guard was going to say.

lines.text: Ash. Don't come to the meeting. Listen to me, don't go. There are six guys in the back of the car park who weren't on the list.
lines.direction: Whispering, panicked, a hand over the phone. Not the same Jojo from the depot.

lines.text: I'll say I couldn't reach you. He's going to know I'm lying. He always knows. Just, please, be somewhere else.
Hey, Ash! It's Jojo. Darius wants to say thank you in person. The public car park, south end. He'd really like you to bring the, uh, the paperwork. All of it. He says to bring all of it.
lines.direction: Bright, jittery, over-rehearsed. He is reading from somebody else's script.

lines.text: Hey. Hey. You came.
lines.direction: Standing by a car, hands too busy, eyes going to the far end of the lot.

lines.text: He does. He's just late.
lines.direction: Flat, the voice of a person lying to a camera.

lines.text: I can't. I can't say. I'm sorry. I really like you, okay? I really like you, so please just run.
It's Jojo. I can't talk long. Walt isn't fishing. He's at the North Point lighthouse. Darius found out an hour ago. They're already on the way.
lines.direction: Whispered, from somewhere echoing. Scared and trying to be brave.

lines.text: Darius. Stop. It's finished. Let them go.
lines.direction: Stepping between them, shaking. His voice is thin and very brave.

lines.text: He came in Tuesdays. Danny Vale. Bought one sour candy and told me the same joke for six years. I never once laughed. He took it very personally.
lines.direction: Behind the counter, polishing a spotless glass. Warm, dry, and entirely serious about it.

lines.text: A mechanic walks into a bar. It gets worse from there.
He left this behind. I've kept it behind the register for five years. Tell Eddie it's not his fault. Tell him in whatever words he'll actually hear.
lines.direction: Setting a small keyring on the counter. A tiny brass wrench.

lines.text: We're out of the good candy. We're always out of the good candy. The good candy is a rumour.
Two kids came by to apologise for the brick. I made them sweep. I've never seen anyone sweep so honestly.
We're open. Mind the glass. Somebody threw a brick last night. I'm told it was kids. Kids with excellent aim and a very good sense of when I've gone home.
lines.direction: Sweeping glass from a shattered window. She does not stop sweeping. Dry, sharp.

lines.text: Thirty-one. Before you ask, I'm not selling.
lines.direction: Looks Ash up and down once, and gives nothing away.

lines.text: Everyone says that. Then a man in a very nice coat comes in and wants to buy.
I signed one thing. A "property assessment access agreement." Nice paper. Nice smile. I didn't read the second page.
lines.direction: A long beat. She takes a folded paper from under the register and doesn't hand it over.

lines.text: Yes. I know. I'm not an idiot. I just didn't have a lawyer, and then I didn't have a window.
lines.direction: Flat. She has known for a week and has not said it aloud.

lines.text: It's very safe. It was perfectly safe until they started making it dangerous.

There's a trailer on the Alder Point site where they keep the property files. A man left a visitor pass on my counter last month and I kept it. Don't ask why. You never know when a woman my age might need to visit a construction site.
And if you meet a woman named Priya Nair at the diner on Cedar, tell her Lucille Ng is finally prepared to be quoted.
lines.direction: Handing over the pass, brisk again.

lines.text: There are two men outside my shop with a van. I'm holding the broom. Come or don't, but the broom and I are going out.
lines.direction: On the phone. Dry, curt, brisk as a slap.

lines.text: They're gone. I didn't even have to hit one. Mostly.
lines.direction: Leaning on the broom among the glass. Out of breath, grinning.

lines.text: I have a very good swing.
Get away from my window! This is a lawful establishment!
lines.direction: Shouting through the door. A woman in the middle of the fight of her life, and enjoying it.

lines.text: I've never been down a day in my life!
A petition. I need twenty names. Three streets. Nobody wants to be the first.
lines.direction: Handing over a clipboard, a pen on a string.

lines.text: I want you to be the one with the transport.
Everyone who can afford the fence.
She once bit a priest.
That's most of them.
The fish thing is in the archive.
Line two, we have Lorraine from Cedar Street.
Hi, Duke, long-time listener, first-time caller.
lines.direction: Now an extremely unconvincing high, quavering older lady. She is clearly doing a voice and is not trying very hard.

lines.text: It's a very bad line.
I just think pigeons should have to carry ID.
lines.direction: The voice again, a little too close to the mic.

lines.text: Three cars left at once.
Police say the cars left at "speeds unsuitable for a car park."
A brisk shuffle, yes.
Warrants for Victor Sloane.
Somebody gave the paper the whole file.
It's very nice.
You said you'd say that at the end of the show.
He ate it.
A fog assessment fee.
He also said that about Tuesdays.
The harbor commission says gulls are "a protected local community." So technically you owe him.
That's not confirmed.
The lighthouse keepers' union says the light "stayed on throughout, as per contract."
The dockworker who was out there is reportedly fine. He asked for a blanket and a sandwich.
We don't have a quiet one.
Two are me. One is my other phone.
lines.direction: Brisk, the voice of someone with three other jobs. Typing as she talks.

lines.text: He left a comment. It says "where is this."
He's calling it, quote, "a hybrid arrangement."
Legal wants me to say they're "previously enjoyed."
It's the most common car.
Another caller says a plate near the King Haulage depot ends in four-four-seven-one.
Ninety.
lines.direction: Reading it again, in case it was a typo.

lines.text: Or somebody phoned it in before anyone got there.
It's a ride. I've been on it.
I was eating a pretzel.
We don't have mugs.
You know, if you drove even slightly worse, I'd be able to teach you things. It's deeply frustrating.
Same black car again. I keep naming them. This one is Gerald.
Okay, so I told Mateo about you. He thinks you're cool. I'm trying very hard not to make it weird.
Obviously.
If you need something, say it. Otherwise I'm busy.
lines.direction: Cool. Not looking up from her phone.

lines.text: I've got a map on my wall. A small one. It has a lot of pins in it. I know it's stupid.
lines.direction: Quiet, once Ash comes close. She says it like a secret.

lines.text: Okay. Before we move anything. Look at this.
lines.direction: Quiet, scanning the car park. A different Mara: attentive, tight.

lines.text: The VIN on the paperwork ends four-four-one-seven. The VIN on the windshield ends four-four-seven-one. Somebody swapped two numbers. Either they're sloppy, or the car isn't the car.
I think I get paid not to think. And so do you.
Did Eddie say anything about this job?
lines.direction: Quick glance at Ash. She says it as if asking about the weather, and it is not.

lines.text: That's Eddie.
lines.direction: A short laugh with no humour in it. She files that away.

lines.text: We do the job. We deliver the car. Anyone asks, the numbers matched, because they always do on the day.
lines.direction: Back to business, deliberately. She is a professional.

lines.text: Mine. Well, theirs. Today. Open the gate, we're expected.
lines.direction: Easy, unbothered, like she has done this a hundred times.

lines.text: The driver. He doesn't talk much. It's the best thing about him.
Okay, stay on my bumper. Not too close, I'm picky about my bumper.
lines.direction: Radio crackle, bright, fast, engine in the background.

lines.text: Public car park, downtown side. Grey sedan, bay on the end of row C. Plates end four-four-seven-one. Somebody is going to leave the key under the mat, because people like that think that's clever.
I know what they pay. That's a different thing.
lines.direction: A tiny pause, a decision about how honest to be.

lines.text: Grey sedan, end of row C. Told you. Key under the mat.
Take it to the King Haulage depot, the one with the high fence on the industrial side. I'll be ahead of you. Drive like you're late for nothing.
The new guy. Eddie says you don't crash. Is that a skill, or just a lack of enthusiasm?
lines.direction: Leaning on the bench, taking Ash in with one sweep. Amused and unimpressed.

lines.text: Cute. I don't hire cute. I hire people who don't stop when things get loud.
It's a car. Pick up, drop off, no questions, and you get paid more than he pays you for a week. I've done it a hundred times. Nothing has ever exploded.
Eddie. Go work on something.
lines.direction: Rolling her eyes, grinning. She likes him.

lines.text: Worry? Every day. Come on, newcomer. You follow me, you don't try to be clever, and if somebody asks, you work for Eddie.
lines.direction: Slight, genuine smile. She picks up her keys.

lines.text: Nice and legal. If a cop gets behind you, you are a very boring person with a very boring car.
Don't look now. Dark car behind the box truck. It's been three turns. Probably nothing. Everything is probably nothing until it isn't.
lines.direction: A little more tension, the same tone.

lines.text: Ash. Where are you? Tell me you're not still in there.
lines.direction: Fast, low, over the radio. She has been listening.

lines.text: That was ninety seconds. Port Alder police don't do ninety seconds. Somebody called it in before you opened the door. Get out. Now.
You're alive. Great. I want that on the record. I'm not paying your funeral.
lines.direction: Out of breath, trying to be light about it. The jokes land short.

lines.text: ...Alder Point. Sloane.
lines.direction: Flips the case. Goes quiet. Very quiet. She reads the page for far too long.

lines.text: Six months ago, three in the morning, I drove a truck from the port to a place that wasn't a place. Nobody said where. The papers on the dash said "Alder Point." I've been watching the docks ever since. This is the first thing I've ever held that looks like what I've been looking for.
lines.direction: Slow, a different, flatter voice. The first time she tells the truth.

lines.text: I didn't tell you my name until Eddie did it for me. I tell people things when I've decided they're useful.
lines.direction: A sharp, tired laugh. Back to her guard.

lines.text: You walked into a rigged warehouse for a stranger and walked out with this. Yeah. You might be.
Darius told you it was his paperwork. This says his money comes from them. That's not an ordinary business arrangement. What do you want to do with it?
lines.direction: Low. Practical. The thinking has already started.

lines.text: Okay.
lines.direction: Very flat. The shutters come down.

lines.text: Then you should know it's the last thing you'll hand him that he can't take back.
lines.direction: Cold, not angry. That is worse.

lines.text: Good. That is the first smart thing anyone has done in this city in a week.
lines.direction: A slow, approving breath, and a small, real smile.

lines.text: You don't know what that means to me.
lines.direction: Quiet. She does not know what to do with her hands. Then she takes a photo of every page.

lines.text: Okay. We do this together. Don't make it weird.
Ash. Where are you? Good. West beach car park. Come alone, take the long way round, and look in your mirrors like you mean it.
lines.direction: Low, fast, outdoors. No jokes. A different Mara.

lines.text: And don't tell Darius you're coming. Don't tell anyone.
I think somebody's been following me since the port. I need a second pair of eyes that doesn't work for Darius.
Rule one of getaways. You never call it a getaway until you're in it.
lines.direction: Driving, eyes on the mirror. Bright, a tight joke to keep the nerves down.

lines.text: Ask me in twenty minutes.
Seatbelt. Left at the pier road, then the coast road. Don't talk, just tell me when they're close.
You're really committing to this.
I've been thinking about my brother the whole time. I think he's been running packages for Darius. And I think somebody told them where I'd be.
lines.direction: Raw. A bit of the truth leaking through the speed.

lines.text: Always.
Hold on. Not my car, not my insurance, not my problem.
That's the last of them. Where's the safest place you know?
lines.direction: Quiet, once the engines fall behind. Out of breath.

lines.text: Same car, three days in a row. Different driver each time. Don't turn around, it's not worth it.
lines.direction: Leaning on her car, not relaxed. Watching a dark sedan parked far down the row.

lines.text: I grew up on these roads. I know every car that doesn't belong.

There was a second page. After the port, I split my notes. I hid a bag at the cove. Receipts, a flash drive, a log of every delivery I could watch. If something happens to me, that bag is the only record.
lines.direction: Practical. She has made a plan and does not want to be told it is a bad one.

lines.text: Because I can't carry it and drive at the same time. And because nobody else has walked into that warehouse and walked out.
And because you didn't hand me a story. You handed me the page.
lines.direction: Softer, a half-smile that vanishes. A thank-you she can't say directly.

lines.text: The cove. We go in my car, I'll drive, you watch the mirrors. If anything looks wrong, you say so. Out loud. Not nicely.
lines.direction: Back to business, car keys already in her hand.

lines.text: I didn't expect anyone to be there.
lines.direction: Sitting on the cot, bag across her knees. Her hands won't stop shaking.

lines.text: Thinking and expecting are different departments.
lines.direction: Dry, brittle. The joke is a wall.

lines.text: Mateo. My little brother. He's seventeen. For a year he's been bringing home cash and telling me it's deliveries for a friend's uncle. I let myself believe him because I needed the money more than I needed the truth.
lines.direction: Quiet, finally. This is the confession.

lines.text: If somebody told Darius where I'd be, it came from someone who knows my life. That's a short list. And Mateo's on it.
I don't know if he's doing it willingly. Or if somebody is making him.
I don't... okay. Okay. Thank you.
lines.direction: A long breath. Her shoulders drop an inch.

lines.text: Right. Sure. You're right. I'll remember that, next time I'm trying not to get my brother killed.
Too close. That's funny. That's my family you're calling too close.
I don't take orders from people I met a week ago.
lines.direction: She stands. Quiet, deliberate. It is not a threat; it is a door closing.

lines.text: Under the concrete step. The lifeguard hut. There.
lines.direction: Low, whispering as if the gulls could hear. Pointing with her chin.

lines.text: Ash. Don't move. Headlights. Two cars. Both pointing at us.
lines.direction: Very still. She is looking at something past Ash's shoulder.

lines.text: They knew exactly where I'd be. Nobody knew I'd be here. Nobody.
lines.direction: Not loud. Almost conversational, which is much worse.

lines.text: "Let's be precise." Who says that? Who actually talks like that?
lines.direction: Perched on the bench, tape recorder in her hands, listening to the tape a second time.

lines.text: You told him. You told the man on the tape what we found.
lines.direction: Cold. She sets the recorder down very carefully.

lines.text: That's the point. You never do.
And you didn't give him everything. Small mercies.
There's a development called Alder Point. Eviction notices on Wharf Street. A shop owner I know. If this is real, the paperwork is in that neighbourhood, not at the port.
lines.direction: Quiet, practical. She has already set the next thing in motion in her head.

lines.text: You know he's going to remember that.
lines.direction: Quiet, once the doors are shut. A smile she can't help.

lines.text: I wasn't sure what you'd do. I'm glad I was wrong.
Twenty thousand.
lines.direction: Cold. Looking out of the window.

lines.text: Not yet.
You were very convincing. I need to know whether that was an act.
Mostly. Great. That's going on my tombstone.
The files are in your jacket. We have to put them somewhere safe. Somewhere that isn't Darius, and isn't police.
Lucille said a woman named Priya Nair would be at the diner on Cedar. She writes for the Ledger. She's the only person in this city who's written a word about Wharf Street.
Headlights at the gate. Two vans. They are not your friendly security. Get to the car.
lines.direction: Hissed, urgent. Somewhere behind her a door slams.

lines.text: Don't speed through the gate, you'll make them remember you. Be a boring man in a boring car. Go.
Wharf Street. Ng's Corner Mart. The owner is a woman called Lucille and she is terrifying. Be polite, and don't touch the candy.
lines.direction: Back to brisk. Something eased since the beach, though she would deny it.

lines.text: Okay. We have a few options and a lot of risk.
lines.direction: Parked outside the diner. Her hand is on the door but she is not opening it.

lines.text: Then let's see if she writes the next one.
You're giving me the only thing that's worth anything.
He is the voice on the tape.
Mr. Sloane.
Ash.
Wow.
lines.direction: A very quiet, very flat laugh that has no humour in it.

lines.text: There it is.
lines.direction: Under her breath, a hard smile.

lines.text: I hope you know what you're doing.
lines.direction: Very low, so only Ash can hear.

lines.text: Lucille. This is Ash. Ash, Lucille Ng. She's run this counter thirty-one years.
lines.direction: Easy, familiar. She has bought candy here since she was nine.

lines.text: Show him the letter, Lucille.
The whole block got the same letter. Four shops, nine apartments. Every one of them has had a window broken, a fire in a bin, or a rumour in the paper that Wharf Street isn't safe.
Trailer by the fence. The pass should get us past the gate guard. Say you're from the lender.
lines.direction: Whisper. The site is quiet, the cranes motionless.

lines.text: Any lender. Developers love lenders.
Public safety. They pay Darius to make it unsafe, and then they pay for the cleanup.
I'm here. What do you need?
That's the scariest thing you could've done.
I saw it on a scanner. Whatever you did, you did it without me. Head for the room. I'll decide when I get there whether to be there.
lines.direction: Distant, cold, but she picked up.

lines.text: I'm two blocks east. I've got the scanner. They're sending three cars, not four, the fourth went for the garage.
lines.direction: Fast, sharp, ready. Engines in the background.

lines.text: Don't go home. Don't go to Eddie. Drive like you're late and make them follow you. I'll clear the street.
Left. Left! Under the highway, they'll lose a block.
You really know how to find trouble. I almost admire it.
I'm not going anywhere. I want that said out loud.
lines.direction: In the doorway. She came the moment she could. Steady.

lines.text: I know. I called him. He's at his friend's place. I told him to stay there and not answer the door. He thinks I'm being dramatic.
I'm done being a person who watches. Whatever we do, we do it together.
Okay. Talk to me. Everything. Not the version where you're a hero. The one where you made choices.
lines.direction: Arms folded, leaning in the doorway. Calm and careful.

lines.text: Prove it. Not with words. With what you do next, because the next thing has my brother in it.
I came to say goodbye. Not to you. To this. I'm taking Mateo and I'm going somewhere that isn't Port Alder.
lines.direction: A bag over her shoulder. Cold, completely composed. She has packed.

lines.text: I'm not leaving you. I'm leaving a mess you chose not to ask me about. You didn't listen, Ash.
One. Because of Mateo. Not because of you.
lines.direction: A hard, tired silence. Then she puts the bag down, slowly.

lines.text: Walt hasn't been to work in six days. His neighbour says he's fishing at the point. Walt doesn't fish. He's hiding. North Point lighthouse.
lines.direction: Fast, working it out as she says it.

lines.text: If Walt kept anything, that's where it is. And if I can work it out, so can Darius.
That's the last piece. Tell me what we're doing with it.
lines.direction: Arriving, winded, hair wild. Looks at the envelope, then at Ash.

lines.text: Dana Whitfield. The one who photographed Rowan's logbook. Okay. Okay, that's a person with a spine.
lines.direction: Slowly. She is impressed in spite of herself.

lines.text: Ash, the only detective you know is on the tape.
That's a lot of faith in a man who says "let's be precise."
Priya. She can't be bought. She can be fired, but she can't be bought.
And when somebody decides to start?
They've got a second set of cars on the coast road. Don't go that way. Cut through the industrial blocks.
lines.direction: Fast, breathless, the engine loud around her.

lines.text: And somebody put in a call. Listen to the scanner. There's a lot of police on the way and none of them for them.
Three cars. They're spreading out for the lighthouse. Don't let them near the door.
lines.direction: Over the radio. Sharp, quick, breathless.

lines.text: That's the spirit. Keep them off him, Ash. Ram them. Smoke them. I don't care, just don't let them get close.
Mateo's at Lucille's. Lucille has a baseball bat and an opinion about everyone who walks in. I've never felt safer about anything.
lines.direction: Pulling a duffel from her car. Crisp. Loose and almost cheerful. A woman who has stopped being afraid of being counted.

lines.text: I'm here for Mateo. After tonight I'll decide what I think of you. Fair?
lines.direction: Arms folded. Professional. A little cool.

lines.text: I'm only here because the alternative is worse. Don't say anything nice. I'll know it's a trick.
lines.direction: Flat. She is on time, and has not forgiven anything.

lines.text: Three stages. The container yard first. PAC-4471 is the container that started this. Whatever's inside is why everyone has been running for six months. We find it, we get it out. Darius will be at the docks, because Darius always is. After that, Sloane.
lines.direction: Straight to it. She spreads a map of the port across the bench.

lines.text: It's not. I just say it with confidence.
lines.direction: A flash of her old grin.

lines.text: If this goes well, I'm going to tell everyone I planned it.
lines.direction: Driving. Dry, to cover the nerves.

lines.text: Mateo got a place on a program in the city. Not the docks. A real one. I looked at the map, and for the first time it didn't look like a trap.
lines.direction: Leaning on the rail at the end of the pier, bag at her feet. Easy, open, the sun on her face. She is smiling, which she does not do often.

lines.text: I'm going for a while. Not leaving. There's a difference. And I thought you might want to come with me and find out what it is.
You did the right thing in the end. I can say that. I can also say I'm not sure how I feel about the road that got us here.
lines.direction: Looking at the water. Careful and honest.

lines.text: Mateo's safe. That's all I'll say about it. For now.
You were right about the evidence. You were wrong about me. I don't think I'll ever stop thinking about both.
lines.direction: At the rail. Cool and distant, a bag already packed.

lines.text: Somewhere that isn't a mess you chose not to ask me about.
The tank's full. I've got a map and a very tired brother. Get in or don't, but you've got about eleven seconds.
lines.direction: Behind the wheel of her car at the end of the East Jetty, engine running. She has Mateo in the back seat, asleep. She grins when she sees Ash, a flash of the old Mara.

lines.text: Anywhere that isn't here.
You burned everything. The whole thing. I want you to know I understand why. I also want you to know I'm not coming with you.
lines.direction: At the jetty, her car already loaded. Mateo sits in the back seat, pretending not to listen. Very cool.

lines.text: That's the nicest thing you've ever said.
He's heading for the bridge. Cut him off or he's gone.
Cars at the gate and cars coming up the service road. We're not going to sit still.
lines.direction: Crisp, calling it. She has taken the wheel.

lines.text: Eddie Vale. Backseat hero.
Don't you dare.
lines.direction: Low, through her teeth. She is standing right behind Ash.

lines.text: You knew him. Eddie. You were in his back room.
lines.direction: Barely a voice. It is not anger; it is grief.

lines.text: Row twelve. Blue door. There it is. PAC-4471.
lines.direction: Whispering. The yard is huge and silent, row after row of containers.

lines.text: Six months. And it's been here the entire time. Sitting in a yard they thought no one would look at.
lines.direction: Very quiet. Her voice cracks on the last word.

lines.text: I need a favour. Not a Darius favour. A clean one. A courier job for the hospital: lab samples from the dealership side. Legal, boring, twelve hundred dollars.
lines.direction: On the phone. Quick, businesslike, a little shy about it.

lines.text: That's a quarter of my ticket out. I've been saving for two years. I'm not telling you why I trust you with it. I'm just telling you I do.
Okay. Twelve hundred. That's thirty-one hundred. I need five. I've started to do the maths in my sleep.
lines.direction: Counting the money into an envelope. She doesn't look up.

lines.text: Out. Me and Mateo. Somewhere with a school he can get into and a street I'm not afraid of. I've got a map on my wall.
lines.direction: Looks up. A flash of something unguarded.

lines.text: Legal speeds. Seatbelt. Pretend you're a nice person. It's good practice.
lines.direction: Light. She can hear the car through the phone.

lines.text: Mateo's at the park. He won't talk to me. He'll talk to you. You're not a sister. You're a stranger. Strangers are easier.
lines.direction: On the phone. Tight, a little ashamed to be asking.

lines.text: Four thousand eight hundred. Two hundred short. I'm going to say it out loud. I'm afraid.
lines.direction: Leaning on her car, a ticket in her hand. The first real calm.

lines.text: Of staying. Of being the person who stayed. What would you do?
You're telling me to leave. And I thought you were going to ask me to stay.
That is manipulative and I love it.
Right. Not fair. Got it.
If my sister told you to check on me, I'm fine. Tell her I'm fine. Tell her loudly.
My sister sent you.
lines.direction: Sitting on the back of a bench with his feet on the seat. Defensive, bored, performing it.

lines.text: She says everything to my face. It's very loud.
Packages. For a friend's uncle.
...Last month one of the packages was heavy in a way it shouldn't have been. I looked. I'm not stupid. I put it back and I didn't say anything.
lines.direction: The performance falters. He stares at his sneakers.

lines.text: Okay. Okay. I'll tell Jojo I'm done.
lines.direction: A long breath. A teenager's deflated shrug that hides a huge relief.

lines.text: Wait. You want me to be, like, a spy?
lines.direction: Surprised. Pleased and scared at once.

lines.text: Don't tell me anything yet. I'm allergic to unconfirmed things. It's a condition.
lines.direction: Typing at a diner table. Doesn't look up.

lines.text: Lucille called me. I've never heard her call anyone.
lines.direction: Sharp, bright, a notebook already open. She has been waiting for a source for a year.

lines.text: Alder Point to King Haulage. Monthly. "Public safety." I've been asking the city for this for fourteen months.
My editor killed the last version of this story. I don't want to lose this one. Will you go on the record?
Then I'll keep it safe. And I'll tell you now, in case it matters later: I only print what holds up.
lines.direction: A short nod. She respects it.

lines.text: Priya. I have two pages written and a lawyer on standby. Give me names, dates and documents, and I'll have a story by midnight that can't be killed.
lines.direction: On speaker. Brisk, bright and tired. Typing in the background.

lines.text: Twenty-three. Lucille asked for twenty. I'm going to put "a few more" in the story, because it sounds stubborn.
lines.direction: Receiving the clipboard, a quick, real smile.

lines.text: There's a permit posted on the Alder Point site fence. If the environmental waiver on it is forged, I can prove it. I need someone to take a photo. Preferably someone who looks like they're supposed to be there.
lines.direction: On the phone. Quick, excited and careful at the same time.

lines.text: A dead man signed the waiver. Ash, do you understand how much easier this makes my life?
lines.direction: Staring at the photo as though it were a diamond.

lines.text: I'll hold it until the rest comes together. And when it does, I'll quote you as "a concerned neighbour". That okay?
Thirty years.
I toured the site. They have a mascot. It's a lighthouse with arms.
I've heard him at the diner. He asked for the salt in a subordinate clause.
I don't want to talk about the fish thing.
Her number is the studio number.
I have footage. It's dark. There's a lot of shouting about a spot.
You called it a shipment of left shoes.
Nobody wants that prize.
Somebody's moved into the tower. High floor. Nobody's seen them.
I filmed it.
It's very good footage. There's a seagull in it.
It's carrying something. Could be a sandwich. Could be paperwork.
What's the benefit?
There's no billing department. It's a drawer.
You fed him a chip first.
He's been filing paperwork.
Gerald.
There's a thermos on the step.
Not a gull.
They're off.
It's Thursday.
